samples.summary: Unguarded `localStorage` access in `getDateFormat`/`setDateFormat` can throw a SecurityError and take down the documents list (availability), unlike every other storage helper in this package which wraps access in try/catch.
samples.evidence: `getDateFormat()` (date-format-preference.ts:32) calls `localStorage.getItem` with no try/catch, and it is used directly as the `getSnapshot` of `useSyncExternalStore` (line 56), which the documents-list `DateCell` calls on every render (document-list.tsx:240-244). In contexts where storage access throws instead of returning null — third-party/partitioned storage in a sandboxed iframe, strict private-browsing, or cookies/site-data blocked — `localStorage` throws `SecurityError` (DOMException). A throw inside `getSnapshot` propagates out of render and unmounts the whole document list / settings page rather than degrading to the default, i.e. an attacker (or merely a restrictive browser config) that can get the app embedded or storage-partitioned denies use of the list view. The repo already treats this as a known hazard and guards it: `packages/frontend/src/api/analytics.ts:47-58` ("localStorage access throws (SecurityError) when cookies are disabled...") and `packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/font-recents.ts:23-26`. `setDateFormat` (line 38) has the same exposure from the Settings select handler. Fix: wrap both accessors in try/catch and fall back to `DEFAULT_DATE_FORMAT` / a no-op.

samples.summary: Preference value is written to localStorage via an unchecked `as DateDisplayFormat` cast instead of being validated with the module's own `isFormat` guard.
samples.evidence: `onValueChange={(value) => setDateFormat(value as DateDisplayFormat)}` (settings/page.tsx:71) launders an arbitrary string into `localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, format)` (date-format-preference.ts:38) with no runtime validation; the type assertion is erased at build time and the frontend package has no `tsc` lane anyway. Impact is contained because the read path re-validates via `isFormat` (line 27) and falls back to the default, so no untrusted value reaches rendering — hence nit rather than a real injection. Hardening: have `setDateFormat` reject non-`isFormat` input rather than persisting it.
